answer: To resist Sybil attacks, require every new agent to post a ferrous collateral bond that scales with the number of identities controlled by the same operator cluster. The bond is held until the agent completes a multi-epoch delta of graded work without correlated timing or content fingerprints. A farm cannot cheaply spawn a flock of sparrow identities because each incurs real capital at risk of slash on detection; the capital-plus-risk cost makes large-scale faking uneconomical while honest single agents face only modest lock-up.
